content.text: : bind to AChE → blocks its action which prevents metabolism of Ach → accumulation of Ach at receptor site → buildup of Ach in synaptic cleft
: inhibit the enzyme AChE, blocking the degradation of ACh, increasing its availability and concentration at all cholinergic receptors (muscarinic and nicotinic)
: GI (N/V/D, abdominal pain), anorexia/weight loss, dizziness, bradycardia, syncope, orthostatic hypotension, QT prolongation
Drug interaction: some AChEIs = CYP substrates
Guidelines: Start low, titrate to target
Pt ed: Gen best tol of AChEIs
MOA: mAbs against amyloid-β plaques → ↑remove amyloid deposits from brain
Early Sx/S AD: mild cognitive impair or mild dementia
Monitoring:  Periodic MRI -risk of ARIA (Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnorm)
ARIA-E = cerebral edema         -    ARIA-H = cerebral microhemorrhage

: selectively binds to the magnesium binding sites within the channel and dissociates very slowly; the pathologic overstimulation and excitotoxic effects of abnormal glutamate neurotransmission are blocked, but normal physiological neurotransmission continues
w.o interfering w physio glut actions
Glut @ NMDA = learning/memory   -chronic/↑stim → Ca influx → neurotox
added when -> mod dz or cont to decline despite AChEI
advancing/progress AD: combo w AChEI + NMDA antagonist

roles.drugs: Cholinesterase inhibitors, equally effective: donepezil is first-line (once daily, well tolerated); rivastigmine (liquid or patch); galantamine (may help behavioral symptoms more). Continue only if function improves after several months
Memantine: moderate to severe disease, alone or with a cholinesterase inhibitor; reduce dose or avoid in renal insufficiency
Selected patients with mild disease (or MCI): anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies (lecanemab, donanemab); modest benefit; ARIA (cerebral edema, microhemorrhage)
